title: Home First Aid Kit
description: Use this list to build or check a household first aid kit based on the American Red Cross list, with extras for bleeding control and long outages.

sources.title: Anatomy of a First Aid Kit
Don't Be Tempted to Use Expired Medicines

items.text: 2 pairs or more of non-latex gloves (large)
Commercial tourniquet from a reputable medical supplier (not a cheap copy) - practice using it
Pressure bandage and compressed or hemostatic gauze for packing deep wounds
2 large absorbent compress dressings (5 x 9 in)
Sterile gauze pads: 5 of 3 x 3 in and 5 of 4 x 4 in
Roller bandages, 3-inch and 4-inch
25 adhesive bandages in assorted sizes
Roll of 1-inch cloth tape
Breathing barrier with one-way valve for CPR
Emergency (space) blanket
Antiseptic wipes (5) and antibiotic ointment packets (5)
Hydrocortisone ointment packets (2)
Instant cold pack
2 triangular bandages for slings and splints
Non-glass, non-mercury thermometer
Tweezers and trauma shears that can cut clothing
2 packets of 81 mg aspirin - for an adult with heart attack signs only, if not allergic and the label or a dispatcher allows; never for children or teens
Printed first aid manual - phones and internet may be down
Household emergency medicines: each person's epinephrine auto-injectors, spare inhaler, and glucose tablets as needed
OTC basics (follow every label): pain and fever reducer, antihistamine, anti-diarrhea medicine, antacid
Oral rehydration salt packets
Saline or clean water bottle for eye wash
Elastic wrap and a moldable splint
Blister supplies, safety pins, penlight, and notepad and pencil for recording times
Child-size bandages and a child-safe fever reducer with its measuring device if you have kids
Store in a cool, dry closet out of children's reach - not the bathroom - and check dates twice a year
Take a hands-on first aid, CPR, and Stop the Bleed class
